q: What is the Doppler effect and what are its applications?
ans: The Doppler effect is the change in perceived frequency of sound (or light) due to relative motion between source and observer. When source approaches, waves are compressed → higher frequency (pitch). Receding: waves stretched → lower frequency. Applications: speed guns, weather radar, medical blood flow measurement (Doppler ultrasound), astronomy (star velocity from red/blue shift).
exp: Doppler: relative motion shifts frequency; approaching → higher f; receding → lower f.
archiveReason: Outside regular CBSE Grade 9 core scope; retained for enrichment/reference.

q: Why is infrasound used for earthquake early warning?
ans: Earthquakes generate infrasound waves that propagate through the Earth's crust. These waves travel faster than the destructive seismic surface waves. Seismographs and infrasound detectors can detect them seconds to minutes before the devastating shaking arrives, giving warning time for evacuation.
exp: Infrasound from earthquakes travels ahead of destructive waves; detected for early warning.

q: How is sound used in the treatment of medical conditions?
ans: Ultrasound is used in: (1) Lithotripsy: focused ultrasound breaks kidney stones. (2) Physiotherapy: therapeutic ultrasound heats deep tissues, promotes healing. (3) Cancer treatment: high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) destroys tumor cells. (4) Dental cleaners: ultrasonic scalers remove tartar. (5) Diagnostic imaging: sonography (prenatal, cardiac, abdominal).
exp: Medical ultrasound: lithotripsy, physiotherapy, HIFU cancer treatment, dental cleaning, diagnostic imaging.

q: What are the advantages of using ultrasound over audible sound for medical imaging?
ans: Higher frequency → shorter wavelength → can image smaller structures (better resolution). Ultrasound is non-ionising (no radiation damage). Can produce real-time moving images (Doppler for blood flow). Can focus on specific tissue layers. Works well in soft tissue. Safe for repeated use and for fetuses during pregnancy.
exp: Ultrasound advantages: short λ → better resolution; non-ionising; real-time; safe; Doppler for blood flow.
archiveReason: Outside regular CBSE Grade 9 core scope; retained for enrichment/reference.

q: Evaluate the role of sound technology in modern medicine.
ans: Ultrasound: diagnostic imaging (most safe, no radiation), Doppler flow measurement, echocardiography. Therapeutic: lithotripsy (kidney stones), HIFU (tumor treatment), physiotherapy. Dental: ultrasonic scaling. Surgical: ultrasonic scalpels. Sound is also used in hearing aids (amplification). These technologies have made diagnosis safer (no X-ray exposure) and enabled non-invasive treatments that replace surgery.
exp: Ultrasound in medicine: diagnosis (sonography, echo), therapy (HIFU, lithotripsy), dental, surgical — non-invasive and radiation-free.
